title: Universal property of module base change
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $M$ be an $R$-module, and let $N$ be an $S$-module with its compatible $R$-module structure. Restriction along $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ gives a bijection between $S$-linear maps $S\otimes_RM\to N$ and $R$-linear maps $M\to N$. Its inverse sends $u:M\to N$ to the unique $S$-linear map with $(s\otimes m)\mapsto s\,u(m)$.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00CV (tensor products of modules), universal property of the tensor product after extension of scalars

mathlib_searches.query: linear maps out of S tensor_R M are equivalent to R-linear maps M to an S-module

mathlib_searches.results: LinearMap.liftBaseChangeEquiv : (M →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[S] (S ⊗[R] M →ₗ[S] N), with tmul and one_tmul formulas

mathlib_match.how: exact pinned Mathlib lines 52-66: LinearMap.liftBaseChangeEquiv (lines 52-53) is the stated bijection; liftBaseChange_tmul (lines 59-60) gives (x ⊗ₜ y) ↦ x • l(y), and liftBaseChangeEquiv_symm_apply (lines 64-66) gives the inverse restriction
